# Explore Suriname

> Independent travel and lifestyle guide to Suriname (South America), written and kept current by people who live there. Covers places to eat, stay and visit, plus live SRD exchange rates, flights, weather and local news. The site is regenerated about every 15 minutes, so rates and schedules stay current.

## Places
- [Restaurants](https://exploresuriname.com/restaurants.html): 189 places to eat across Suriname, spanning Creole, Hindustani, Javanese, Chinese and Maroon cooking.
- [Hotels and Lodges](https://exploresuriname.com/hotels.html): 125 options, from Paramaribo city hotels to interior jungle lodges reached by boat or small plane.
- [Things to Do](https://exploresuriname.com/activities.html): 119 nature parks, tours, attractions and experiences in one list, including UNESCO-listed rainforest, Brownsberg, Galibi, Bigi Pan, river trips, birdwatching and Maroon and Indigenous village visits.
- [Shopping](https://exploresuriname.com/shopping.html): 355 shops, malls and markets.
- [Markets in Suriname](https://exploresuriname.com/markets-in-suriname): which market is on which day: the Centrale Markt, the Maroon market, farmers' markets in Kwatta and Wanica and the Sunday markets of Paramaribo.
- [Local Services](https://exploresuriname.com/services.html): 640 banks, pharmacies, salons and other everyday services.
- [Events and Festivals](https://exploresuriname.com/events.html): annual festivals, public holidays and one-off events, with dates.

## Travel guides
- [The Basics](https://exploresuriname.com/visitor-guide.html): visas, customs, SIM cards, money, ATMs and getting around for first-time visitors.
- [Is Suriname Safe?](https://exploresuriname.com/is-suriname-safe.html): practical safety guidance for tourists.
- [Entry Requirements](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-entry-requirements): the Entry Fee, e-visas, the mandatory ICF form, passport rules and exemptions.
- [Customs](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-customs): cash limit, duty-free allowances, food, medicines, pets and what may not be taken out.
- [Health](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-health): vaccinations, malaria-free status, dengue and chikungunya, tap water and hospitals.
- [Getting Around](https://exploresuriname.com/getting-around-suriname): taxis, minibuses, car rental, boats and flights to the interior.
- [Best Time to Visit](https://exploresuriname.com/best-time-to-visit-suriname): dry and rainy seasons month by month, turtles and festivals.
- [About Suriname](https://exploresuriname.com/about-suriname): country fact file: geography, climate, population and ethnic groups, languages, religion, history, government, economy, nature, the ten districts, national symbols, public holidays and practical facts.
- [History of Suriname](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-history.html): interactive timeline of Surinamese history, from the first Indigenous peoples through slavery and Keti Koti to independence and the oil era, in English and Dutch.
- [Flora & Fauna of Suriname](https://exploresuriname.com/flora-fauna/): every animal, plant and fungus recorded in Suriname (about 18,500 species, 4,000 profiles) with names in English, Dutch, Spanish, Chinese, Sranan Tongo and Latin, where each species has been recorded by district, photos and sources.
- [Suriname Itinerary](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-itinerary.html): suggested multi-day routes combining Paramaribo and the interior.
- [Driving and Traffic](https://exploresuriname.com/on-the-road.html): driving, road rules, a live traffic map and emergency numbers.

## Recipes
- [Surinamese Recipes](https://exploresuriname.com/recipes): home recipes for Surinamese dishes in English, Dutch, Spanish, Chinese, French and Portuguese, from Creole, Hindostani, Javanese and Chinese-Surinamese kitchens.
- [Bami: Surinamese-Javanese Fried Noodles](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-bami): Spaghetti stir-fried with onion, garlic, laos, trassi and sweet and salty soy, finished with celery leaf. A Surinamese party and warung classic.
- [Bruine bonen met rijst (BB met R): Surinamese Brown Beans with Chicken and Rice](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-bruine-bonen-met-rijst): Brown beans stewed with chicken, zoutvlees, tomato, celery and a whole Madame Jeanette pepper, served over white rice.
- [Heri heri: Boiled Tubers and Plantain with Salt Cod](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-heri-heri): A humble Creole classic: cassava, sweet potato and green and ripe plantain with a spicy stew of bakkeljauw. A Keti Koti favourite.
- [Kousenband met zoutvlees: Surinamese Yardlong Beans with Salted Beef](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-kouseband-met-zoutvlees): Yardlong beans stewed with zoutvlees, onion, garlic and tomato: the classic Surinamese vegetable dish to eat with white rice.
- [Kwie kwie: Surinamese Stewed Armoured Catfish](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-kwie-kwie): Armoured swamp catfish stuffed with zoutvlees, browned in oil and slowly stewed with tomato, onion and a whole hot pepper.
- [Moksi alesi: Surinamese Mixed Rice with Salted Beef and Salt Cod](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-moksi-alesi): Surinamese one-pot rice cooked with zoutvlees, bakkeljauw, onion and tomato, with a whole Madame Jeanette pepper for aroma.
- [Nasi: Surinamese Fried Rice](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-nasi): Surinamese-Javanese nasi goreng: cold rice fried with shredded chicken, laos, kentjoer and ketjap. Serve with omelette, cucumber and sambal.
- [Pastei: Surinamese Chicken Pie](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-pastei): Surinamese chicken pie with carrots, peas, capers and nutmeg in a buttery crust, a festive classic at birthdays and family parties.
- [Pom: Surinamese Chicken and Tayer Bake](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-pom): Suriname's festive oven dish: grated tayer root layered with chicken and salted beef, baked until golden with a dark, crisp crust.
- [Roti: Surinamese Split-Pea Flatbread with Masala Chicken](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-roti): Classic Surinamese roti with a spiced split-pea filling, served with masala chicken and potatoes. A Hindostani favourite loved by all.
- [Bakkeljauw gestoofd: Surinamese Stewed Salt Cod in Tomato](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-bakkeljauw-gestoofd): Salt cod stewed with onion, garlic, tomato and hot pepper: a Surinamese staple for bread rolls, rice, cassava or heri heri.
- [Teloh met bakkeljauw: Fried Cassava with Salt Fish](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-teloh-met-bakkeljauw): Golden fried cassava with salted cod fried with garlic, hot pepper, onion and tomato. A favourite Surinamese warung lunch.
- [Tjauw min: Surinamese-Chinese Fried Noodles](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-tjauw-min): Yellow egg noodles stir-fried with onion, garlic and soy sauce, tossed with kaisoi and topped with Chinese roast pork and fachong.
- [Vis in kokossaus: Fish in Turmeric Coconut Sauce](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-vis-in-kokossaus): Chunks of fish fillet gently stewed in coconut milk with ginger, kunir and salam leaves, with golden slices of fried pumpkin.
- [Zuurkool met zoutvlees: Surinamese Stewed Sauerkraut with Salted Beef](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-zuurkool-met-zoutvlees): Sauerkraut stewed the Surinamese way with zoutvlees, onion, garlic, tomato and plenty of black pepper, served with white rice.
- [Cassavesoep: Surinamese Cassava Soup with Salted Beef](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-cassavesoep): A clear, peppery broth of soup beef and zoutvlees with allspice and leaf celery, ladled over tender cubes of cassava.
- [Okersoep met tomtom: Surinamese Okra Soup with Plantain Dumplings](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-okersoep-met-tomtom): Hearty Creole okra soup with tayer leaves, chicken, salted beef and dried fish, served with tomtom: soft pounded plantain balls.
- [Peprewatra: Surinamese Peppery Fish Soup](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-peprewatra): A light, clear fish broth with allspice, bay leaf and a whole Madame Jeanette pepper. Quick, restorative and full of flavour.
- [Pindasoep: Surinamese Peanut Soup](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-pindasoep): Creamy Surinamese peanut soup with chicken, salted beef and allspice, scented with a whole Madame Jeanette pepper. Best with tomtom.
- [Saoto: Surinamese-Javanese Chicken Soup](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-saoto): Fragrant chicken broth poured over shredded chicken, crisp potato, fried vermicelli and bean sprouts. Suriname's favourite Javanese soup.
- [Boulanger gestoofd: Surinamese Stewed Aubergine](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-boulanger-gestoofd): Aubergine cubes stewed with onion, garlic and tomato until soft and creamy, seasoned with black pepper. A simple Surinamese side for rice.
- [Goedangan: Javanese Vegetables with Coconut Sambal](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-goedangan): Blanched cabbage, yard-long beans, bean sprouts and greens with a spicy coconut sambal. A fresh Surinamese-Javanese side dish.
- [Nasi koening: Surinamese-Javanese Yellow Rice](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-nasi-koening): Rice cooked in coconut milk with turmeric, coriander, salam leaves and lemongrass. Fragrant yellow rice for fish, chicken and festive meals.
- [Petjil: Javanese Vegetables with Peanut Sauce](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-petjil): Crisp blanched yard-long beans, cabbage, bean sprouts and greens under a thick, spicy peanut sauce. Simple Surinamese-Javanese comfort food.
- [Sopropo met zoutvlees: Surinamese Bitter Gourd with Salted Beef](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-sopropo-met-zoutvlees): Bitter gourd sliced thin, salted to tame the bitterness and stewed with zoutvlees, onion, tomato and soy sauce. A Surinamese side for rice.
- [Bakabana: Surinamese Plantain Fritters](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-bakabana): Slices of very ripe plantain fried in a light batter until golden, a favourite Surinamese snack served with peanut sauce.
- [Bara: Surinamese Savoury Urdi Doughnuts](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-bara): Puffy, golden Surinamese bara made with urdi meal, garlic, cumin and pepper, fried until crisp and eaten warm with chutney.
- [Manja met lotis: Green Mango with Spicy Ketjap Dip](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-manja-met-lotis): Tart green mango dipped in lotis, a sweet, salty and fiery sauce of pounded pepper, brown sugar and ketjap. A Surinamese favourite.
- [Phulauri: Surinamese Split-Pea Fritters](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-phulauri): Crisp Surinamese phulauri: fritters of soaked, ground yellow split peas with garlic, cumin and pepper, served with hot sauce or chutney.
- [Pommerak met zout: Malay Apple with Salt and Vinegar](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-pommerak-met-zout): Juicy pommerak wedges tossed with salt and a dash of vinegar: a simple, refreshing fruit snack straight from the Surinamese yard.
- [Bojo: Surinamese Cassava and Coconut Cake](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-bojo): Moist Surinamese cake of grated cassava and coconut with cinnamon, vanilla, almond and raisins. No flour needed and naturally gluten-free.
- [Cassave dokun: Steamed Cassava and Coconut Parcels](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-cassave-dokun): Sweet Surinamese parcels of grated cassava, coconut, cinnamon and raisins, wrapped in banana leaf and steamed until firm.
- [Fiadu: Surinamese Fruit and Almond Pastry](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-fiadu): Festive Surinamese yeast pastry: buttery swirls filled with cinnamon sugar, rum-soaked raisins, candied peel and almonds.
- [Jalebi: Crisp Fried Spirals in Sugar Syrup](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-jalebi): Bright orange Surinamese jalebi: crisp fried spirals of yogurt batter soaked in sugar syrup. A Hindostani sweet, eaten warm or cold.
- [Keksi: Surinamese Sponge Cake](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-keksi): Light Surinamese keksi: an airy cinnamon and vanilla sponge, brushed with butter while warm and topped with sugar sprinkles.
- [Sambal: Surinamese Madame Jeanette Pepper Sambal](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-sambal-madame-jeanette): Homemade Surinamese sambal of Madame Jeanette peppers, onion, sugar and trassi, slowly fried until thick. Hot, fragrant and a little sweet.
- [Zuurgoed: Surinamese Pickled Cucumber](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-zuurgoed): Cucumber in vinegar with Madame Jeanette pepper, cloves and allspice: the sharp, spicy side for moksi alesi, bami and nasi.
- [Dawet: Surinamese Coconut Milk Drink with Lemongrass Syrup](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-dawet): Chilled coconut milk over sweet sereh syrup with soft cornstarch drops: the Javanese-Surinamese drink for hot days and parties.
- [Gemberbier: Surinamese Ginger Beer](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-gemberbier): Homemade non-alcoholic Surinamese ginger beer with fresh ginger, cloves and a touch of cola-essence, served ice cold.
- [Orgeade: Surinamese Almond Syrup](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-orgeade): Homemade almond syrup from sweet and bitter almonds, boiled up three times and bottled. Dilute with ice-cold water to serve.
- [Serehthee: Surinamese Lemongrass Tea](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-serehthee): Hot tea of fresh lemongrass leaves, sweetened with honey. Fragrant, simple and drunk all over Suriname.
- [Tamarindestroop: Surinamese Tamarind Syrup](https://exploresuriname.com/recipe-tamarindestroop): Sweet and tangy homemade tamarind syrup, steeped for two days and bottled. Dilute with cold water and ice for a classic Surinamese drink.

## Order food
- [Order KFC in Suriname](https://exploresuriname.com/kfc): how to order KFC in Suriname for delivery or pickup through its WhatsApp order line, the menu, and every KFC restaurant in Suriname with address, phone number and directions.
- [Order Pizza Hut in Suriname](https://exploresuriname.com/pizza-hut): how to order Pizza Hut in Suriname for delivery or pickup through its WhatsApp order line, the menu, and every Pizza Hut restaurant in Suriname with address, phone number and directions.

## Live data
- [SRD Exchange Rates](https://exploresuriname.com/currency.html): Surinamese Dollar rates from CBVS (the central bank, official reference) and CME (the cash market). The cash rate is what travellers actually receive at exchange offices in Paramaribo, not the mid-market rate shown by global currency converters.
- [Flights](https://exploresuriname.com/flights.html): arrivals and departures for Johan Adolf Pengel International (PBM) and Eduard Alexander Gummels (EAX) airports.
- [Weather and Tides](https://exploresuriname.com/conditions.html): seven-day district forecasts, river tidal predictions and sunrise and sunset times.
- [Daily Notices](https://exploresuriname.com/daily-notices.html): on-call pharmacies, power and water outage notices, and cinema showtimes.
- [Gas Cylinder Finder](https://exploresuriname.com/gas-cylinders): the nearest Ogane sale points to swap a 20 or 28 lbs cooking gas cylinder (map and nearest-to-me), the official refill prices, and how to order 40 and 100 lbs cylinders with delivery days per neighbourhood.
- [ATM Finder](https://exploresuriname.com/atms.html): every ATM in Suriname on a map with live up/down status where the bank publishes it, plus which cards each machine accepts (BNETS, Mastercard, Visa, foreign cards).
- [Live Scores](https://exploresuriname.com/matches.html): live scores and fixtures in Suriname time (UTC-3): Natio Suriname internationals (men, women, youth), the Suriname Major League with results and the official table, the Concacaf Caribbean Cup, Oranje and Brazil, world football (Champions League, Premier League, Eredivisie, World Cup when it runs and more), NBA games, India and West Indies cricket, Formula 1 and fight nights (UFC, Glory Kickboxing, boxing), plus recent results.
- [Suriname Time and World Clock](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-time.html): current Suriname time (UTC-3, no daylight saving), a live world-clock band and a two-way time-zone converter with a Netherlands call-overlap helper.

## Oil and gas
- [Suriname Oil and Gas Overview](https://exploresuriname.com/oil-and-gas.html): the whole sector in one page. Suriname has no offshore production yet; first oil from the GranMorgu development in Block 58 is targeted for 2028, while onshore fields produce around 17,000 barrels a day. Includes live Brent crude and the latest sector headlines.
- [Offshore Blocks and Operators](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-oil-blocks.html): block-by-block table of who operates what offshore Suriname (TotalEnergies on Block 58, PETRONAS on Block 52, APA on Block 53, Chevron and Shell in shallow and deep acreage), the discovery-well record and the Open Door Offering.
- [The GranMorgu Project](https://exploresuriname.com/granmorgu.html): Suriname's first offshore oil development. US$10.5 billion sanctioned in October 2024, a 220,000 barrel per day FPSO, up to 32 wells, TotalEnergies 40% / APA 40% / Staatsolie 20%, first oil targeted 2028.
- [Oil Timeline and Roadmap](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-oil-timeline.html): from the 1928 traces and Staatsolie's founding in 1980 to the 2020 discoveries, the 2024 final investment decision, first oil in 2028 and possible first gas around 2030.
- [Petroleum Contracts and Fiscal Terms](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-oil-contracts.html): how Suriname's production sharing contracts work, the 6.25% royalty, cost oil and profit oil, the 36% income tax, Staatsolie's 20% back-in right, past bid rounds and how to bid.
- [Who Governs the Oil](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-oil-government.html): the Ministry of Oil, Gas and Environment (created 2025, Minister Patrick Brunings), Staatsolie, the National Environment Authority and the Savings and Stabilisation Fund, plus what the IMF says is unfinished.
- [Oil and Gas Jobs and Local Content](https://exploresuriname.com/suriname-oil-jobs.html): supplier registration through the SSRP and SAP Ariba, offshore safety and NATIN training routes, realistic job expectations and why Suriname still has no local content law.

## Daily games
- [Sabi Suriname](https://exploresuriname.com/quiz.html): free daily five-question quiz about Suriname, in Dutch and English.
- [Switi Mini](https://exploresuriname.com/crossword.html): daily Surinamese mini crossword with mixed Dutch, Sranan and English clues.
- [Pe A De?](https://exploresuriname.com/map-game.html): daily map game; tap the official map of Suriname (Tigri area included) to locate five real places.
- [Korjaal Run](https://exploresuriname.com/korjaal.html): arcade river runner from Atjoni upriver; switch lanes, jump logs and kaaimannen, duck branches, finish missions.
- [Aboma](https://exploresuriname.com/anaconda.html): snake game in stages from Bigi Pan to the Nickerie polders; eat pirai and kwikwi, dodge kaaimannen.
- [Muskieto Survivor](https://exploresuriname.com/muskieto.html): five-minute terras survival game; auto-firing mepper, Mama's slipper and Madame Jeanette against muskieto swarms.
- [Heiligenweg Jam](https://exploresuriname.com/heiligenweg-jam): bus-jam puzzle at Paramaribo's bus station; tap lijnbussen out of the lot so passengers board the bus home. Endless levels.

## Business
- [Doing Business in Suriname](https://exploresuriname.com/doing-business-in-suriname): short orientation for business visitors and investors: currency, business language, time zone, company registration (KKF), BTW, minimum wage and main sectors.
- Business calculators, invoice and document makers, government tenders, job vacancies and business guides are on the sister site [SurinameBusiness.com](https://surinamebusiness.com/en/) (Dutch version at https://surinamebusiness.com/).
